topic.title: Merge Tool
topic.shortdesc: Use the merge tool to compare versions of a file and merge changes into the current document.

body.p: includes a file merge tool. It is useful when multiple users work on the same documents at the same time because it helps resolve conflicts when you commit changes to a repository. It performs a three-way comparison to show the differences between your local version of a document and the latest version committed to the repository by another user since your last commit.

section.title: Triggering the Merge Tool
section.p:
The Web Author merge tool is activated in the following ways:
It is triggered when you select Compare with Latest version from repository or Compare with Another file from the More drop-down menu in the main toolbar.
These actions open the Merge dialog box if the editor is not read-only. Otherwise, the file comparison tool opens.
After you close the dialog box, changes that you merge into the file in the left pane are synchronized with the main editor.
When you commit a file to a Git repository and there is a conflict, you are presented with the choice to Merge and Commit or Commit to a new branch. If you choose Merge and Commit, the merge tool opens so that you can review and resolve the conflict.
When Web Author is integrated with a CMS, the merge tool can be triggered based on an configuration specified by the CMS.

section.title: Using the Merge Tool
section.p: The merge tool displays two files side by side with lines and colored highlights that help you visualize the differences. The file in the left pane is your local version and can be edited, so differences can be merged into it. The file in the right pane is the latest version committed to the repository by another user and cannot be edited. Differences between the files are highlighted, and you can navigate between them by using the arrow buttons on the toolbar (, , , ) or by clicking the highlights on the vertical stripe on the right side. If a base file is provided, the tool performs a three-way comparison.

The toolbar also includes a Tags Display Mode drop-down button that lets you select how many tags to display for XML files and a Toggle Text Mode button to show differences in the XML source (text mode). When showing differences in text mode, the toolbar contains a Toggle Ignore Whitespaces button that turns whitespace ignoring on or off.

To merge the changes, you can use the following functions:
Use the Copy Change from Right to Left toolbar button to copy a specific change or block of changes from the file in the right pane to the left pane.
Use the Copy All Changes from Right to Left toolbar button to copy all changes from the file in the right pane to the left pane. If a three-way merge is performed and the editor identifies conflicts, the action copies only non-conflicting changes.
You can also edit the content in the left pane manually by using features such as:
Insert new elements using the Content Completion menu (triggered when pressing Enter).
Editing actions can be triggered using various keyboard shortcuts (e.g. Ctrl+Z for undo, Ctrl+Y for redo, Ctrl+C for copy, Ctrl+V for paste, Ctrl+B for bold, Ctrl+U for underline, etc.).
Various editing actions are also available from the contextual menu.
Editing and styling actions can also be triggered easily by using the Floating Contextual Toolbar.
Find and replace content by using Ctrl+F to trigger a Find/Replace dialog box.
Add and remove attributes using actions from the contextual menu.
Comment and change tracking actions (e.g. Add Comment, Delete Comment, Reply, Accept Changes, Reject Changes) are available in the contextual menu.

After you make changes in the file in the left pane, new differences between the two files may appear. The visual highlights for these differences can become out of date. By default, the visual highlights are updated automatically when you make changes to the document. For large documents, this update can take a long time and affect the user experience, so the editor can be configured to disable this behavior by using the &runDiffOnChange=false URL parameter. In this case, a Re-compute Differences button appears on the toolbar to update the visual highlights.
